prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators, and its experimental observation in HgTe quantum wells

statement.case_for: I opened with active matter (B005) because it fits my own taste for a simple universal mechanism, but I do not think my personal taste should decide a prize that five colleagues ranked in their top eight and three put in their top three. B042 is the strongest candidate where the mechanism is simple, general and also confirmed by nature. Kane and Mele showed that time-reversal symmetry plus spin-orbit coupling allows a Z2 invariant, so that a band insulator carries protected edge or surface states. This is a clean statement about band topology, and it was not a repackaging of the integer quantum Hall effect. Molenkamp's group then observed the helical edge channels in HgTe quantum wells, giving the quantized conductance the theory required. The idea has since been confirmed in many materials (HgTe, InAs/GaSb, Bi-based compounds by ARPES) and is well understood, so the field is mature rather than speculative. It is also a prediction-then-measurement chain, which is what makes it a discovery and not only a framework.
statement.case_against: Credit is the weak point. The Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal is what directed Molenkamp's group to HgTe, and Zhang is deceased, so the prize cannot recognise that step. Fu, Kane and Mele, Moore and Balents, and Roy on the three-dimensional case, and Hasan's ARPES demonstration of a 3D topological insulator, all fall outside the three-name cap. The 2016 prize for topological phase transitions also makes some colleagues wary of returning to topology so soon. If the committee cannot accept the omissions, B037, which has an unusually clean two-person attribution, is the better choice, and I would not stand in the way of it.

responses.point: Johansson ranks B042 third but warns that omitting Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang is a real allocation problem, and that the 2016 topological prize may make the committee reluctant to return to the area.
responses.response: I agree the BHZ omission is real, and I would not say it is resolved. But the BHZ paper is a proposal that predicted the HgTe quantum well would host the effect, and the underlying concept and the Z2 invariant come from Kane and Mele. A prize citing the quantum spin Hall effect and its observation can be written so that it honours the idea and the decisive experiment without claiming to list all who contributed. On 2016, Thouless, Haldane and Kosterlitz honoured topological phase transitions and the integer-quantized Hall conductance. Time-reversal-invariant topological insulators with protected helical edges are a distinct result, not covered by that citation, so I do not think the overlap is disqualifying.

responses.point: Eriksson ranks B018 first and B042 second, and treats B042 as a well confirmed, overdue idea but warns that priority around BHZ, Fu-Kane-Mele and Moore-Balents and the 3D discovery by Hasan makes a three-person split contentious. He also notes the overlap with B012.
responses.response: I agree with the priority concern and think it is the central difficulty. On B012 versus B042, I prefer the narrower B042 framing. Xue's quantum anomalous Hall realisation depends on magnetic doping and is a separate result, and bundling it into one prize would make a compound citation that is harder to defend scientifically. On B018, I find the Bistritzer-MacDonald flat-band picture elegant, but the pairing mechanism and the nature of the correlated phases are not understood, so I would still put it behind B042 on maturity: we would be rewarding a platform whose physics is still being interpreted.

responses.point: Kroll ranks B037 first: optical lattice clocks at the 1e-18 level are an unambiguous invention with a clean two-laureate attribution, and he treats overlap with the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-clock prizes as the main risk.
responses.response: This is the strongest competing case and I take it seriously. The attribution for Katori and Ye is cleaner than for B042, and I accept that point. My reservation is conceptual, not about maturity. The magic-wavelength idea is clever and the metrology is superb, but a large part of the value is the engineering of systematic uncertainty, and the new fundamental-physics result (a test of constants or relativistic geodesy) is still prospective. I also share your worry about the neighbouring prizes of 2005 and 2012. I rank B037 as my first alternative because the attribution risk of B042 is higher, and if the committee puts a premium on clean credit I would accept it.

responses.point: Lindroth ranks B037 first, and values the close agreement between theory and experiment in precision atomic physics. She openly relies on memory for the priority history of the magic-wavelength proposal and defers on condensed matter, ranking B042 fifth.
responses.response: I would ask that the priority history of the magic-wavelength proposal be checked against the primary papers before the final ballot, since it is the foundation of the B037 attribution, and I would say the same for B042's BHZ question. On your point about closing the loop between theory and experiment, B042 meets that standard as well: the Z2 prediction and the HgTe measurement of quantized edge conductance are exactly that kind of agreement. I understand you defer on condensed matter, so the question is whether the committee can address the credit issues in B042 without a specialist who ranks it first.

uncertainties: Whether the theory credit can be fairly limited to Kane and Mele, given Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang (with Zhang deceased), Fu-Kane-Mele and Moore-Balents, and the 3D experiments.
Whether the 2016 topological prize and the 2010 graphene prize make the committee reluctant to reward topology or two-dimensional materials again.
The priority history of the magic-wavelength proposal for B037 and the exact originality of the B042 theory timeline have not been verified from primary sources in this exercise.
Whether a statistical-physics or soft-matter prize such as B005 can gain support beyond my own ranking; at present it cannot.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile with any shortlisted candidate or credited name. I note only that I am in the Gothenburg physics environment with Johansson and Olsson (Chalmers), with no specific collaboration found; this does not require recusal.
